entry.content:
Discussion split between architecture theory, benchmark rigor, and AI's economic impact. Yann LeCun set the technical tone by clarifying JEPA taxonomy, while Artificial Analysis anchored methodology talk with its Decision Index v2 launch.

  • Yann LeCun explained the P in JEPA means predictive, mapping when joint-embedding architectures need predictors versus generative designs
  • Greg Brockman argued test-time-compute frontier models now drive scientific discovery, echoing Shunyu Yao's claim that AI will soon master biology via autonomous labs
  • Ethan Mollick flagged benchmark-fragility research showing trivial edits, like renaming files, can distort coding leaderboard rankings
  • levelsio retired Infinite Slop TV after 17.8M clip views and showed AI compressing i18n work to minutes; Gary Marcus countered that jobs and productivity barely moved

entry.title: @TimDarcet @gabriberton The P in JEPA stands for predictive. The main distinction is not between JEA...
entry.summary: LeCun continues yesterday's Social thread, adding formal loss formulations and the history of anti-collapse methods. Yann LeCun (@ylecun) responds to a discussion by clarifying the taxonomy of joint-embedding architectures: the P in JEPA stands for predictive, and the fundamental distinction is not between JEA and JEPA but between joint-embedding approaches (predictive or not) and generative architectures. He lays out formal loss formulations: generative models predict y from x with a divergence loss between target and prediction, while JEA encodes both x and y and minimizes representation divergence with an anti-collapse regularizer R, useful when neither view has a privileged direction (e.g., two views of the same scene). He adds historical depth, citing Becker and Hinton's 1989 information-maximization anti-collapse model and noting Schmidhuber's early related work, and notes that whether a predictor is needed depends on the task.

entry.title: AA-Paperclip tests models on extracting facts and making decisions about real-world documents. Each ...

entry.title: AA-Symmetry measures how consistent models are when asked equivalent questions. We take a fixed task...

entry.title: Decision model costs ranged from $14 per 1M Tasks for Celeris-1.1 Decision to $859 for Clef. Celeris...
entry.summary: Cost analysis of decision models: $14 per 1M tasks for Celeris-1.1 Decision up to $859 for Clef, with Pareto frontier analysis including GPT-6 Luna and Claude Haiku 5.5 at the high end. Explains how multi-pass billing inflates effective cost, e.g. GLiDE v1.2 at $780 per 1M tasks despite cheap token pricing.

entry.title: @bernhardsson Price on its own says nothing about revenue. In both cases the important variable is d...
entry.summary: Francois Chollet responds to Bo Bernhardsson in a discussion about AI pricing and revenue, arguing that price alone is not informative — demand structure is the key variable. He explains that revenue can rise both when price rises and when it falls because there is a core of price-insensitive demand alongside a large pool of price-sensitive latent demand; higher prices extract more from the former, lower prices unlock the latter.

entry.title: Social Summary: November 08, 2026
entry.summary:
Agentic coding and AI-designed physical products dominated the conversation. Andrej Karpathy demoed TristanTube, a 47K-video app one-shotted with Claude Code, while levelsio's viral AI-furniture thread spawned a broader thesis on personal hardware and new maker markets.

  • Francois Chollet argued data/compute scaling is a multiplier on generalization, not a substitute — intersecting with Yann LeCun's detailed SSL/JEPA taxonomy and Gary Marcus's chart calling Anthropic's growth projections fantasy
  • Perplexity CEO Arav Srinivas shared breakout Teammate launch metrics (3.7x day-two automation growth) and claimed instant PMF as a chief-of-staff assistant
  • Ethan Mollick was highly prolific: amplifying new Anthropic research that AI could absorb 27–52% of researcher time, arguing human fact-checking of AI output is becoming obsolete, and pitching AI-enabled investigative journalism
  • Jim Fan teased an 'extraordinary' CoRL keynote two days out and vouched that a robot demo was genuinely autonomous at real speed
  • Greg Brockman's cryptic note that security architecture matters more than ever reflected rising security anxiety among frontier-lab leaders
entry.content:
Agentic coding and AI-designed physical products dominated the conversation. Andrej Karpathy demoed TristanTube, a 47K-video app one-shotted with Claude Code, while levelsio's viral AI-furniture thread spawned a broader thesis on personal hardware and new maker markets.

  • Francois Chollet argued data/compute scaling is a multiplier on generalization, not a substitute — intersecting with Yann LeCun's detailed SSL/JEPA taxonomy and Gary Marcus's chart calling Anthropic's growth projections fantasy
  • Perplexity CEO Arav Srinivas shared breakout Teammate launch metrics (3.7x day-two automation growth) and claimed instant PMF as a chief-of-staff assistant
  • Ethan Mollick was highly prolific: amplifying new Anthropic research that AI could absorb 27–52% of researcher time, arguing human fact-checking of AI output is becoming obsolete, and pitching AI-enabled investigative journalism
  • Jim Fan teased an 'extraordinary' CoRL keynote two days out and vouched that a robot demo was genuinely autonomous at real speed
  • Greg Brockman's cryptic note that security architecture matters more than ever reflected rising security anxiety among frontier-lab leaders

entry.title: Data scaling and compute scaling are *multipliers* for the generalization power of an approach. Tril...
entry.summary: Francois Chollet argues that data and compute scaling are multipliers on an approach's generalization power rather than a substitute for it; massive investment can make low-generalization methods look adequate, but a cleverer approach will scale better. He advises researchers to work on methods that can scale while remembering scaling alone is not the end-all of AI.

entry.title: Earlier this week Tristan published his top YouTube channels: https://t.co/NZ3UCNo6cT Which looked e...
entry.summary: Karpathy showcases TristanTube, a 47K-video YouTube-style viewer built from a curated channel list, stating it was one-shotted with Claude Code in about three minutes.

entry.title: @gabriberton Several comments: 1. image/video SSL methods differ by whether they use reconstruction ...
entry.summary: Yann LeCun provides a detailed technical taxonomy of self-supervised learning methods: distinguishing reconstruction-based from joint-embedding approaches, explaining that DINO is technically a JEA (a kind of JEPA) differing in anti-collapse criterion and augmentation, situating V-JEPA 2.1 as a corporate-lab effort, and separating research papers like LeJEPA from applied/fine-tuned work.

entry.title: Claude Code can design furniture part by part and then give you a bill of materials to order each pa...
entry.summary: levelsio's viral post describes using Claude Code to design furniture part by part and produce a bill of materials for ordering cheap parts directly from suppliers, bypassing heavily marked-up furniture brands (citing a $30,000 sofa). He notes Opus 5.5 and other models can operate free 3D tools like Blender and FreeCAD, making self-designed furniture practical, and that a non-designer, non-coder (@theannalux) designed a table from scratch working with Claude Code in the terminal, which he argues is superior to the app.

entry.title: Teammate automation runs grew 3.7x from launch day to day two. This is despite day two being a Frida...
entry.summary: Continuing our coverage of the Perplexity Teammates rollout, Perplexity CEO Arav Srinivas shares adoption metrics for the newly launched Teammate product, reporting automation runs grew 3.7x from launch day to day two despite it being a Friday, and predicts accelerating productivity gains for high-agency professionals.

entry.title: Some new data from Anthropic looking at the impact of AI on the sciences by field: "With current cap...
entry.summary: Mollick highlights new Anthropic research finding that, with current capabilities and wide adoption, AI could take on 27-52% of researcher time needed to produce a new study, with a median of 38% across fields, linking the source.

entry.title: I think there is way too much concern expressed about verification of AI output in everyday work due...
entry.summary: Ethan Mollick argues that excessive concern about verifying AI output for factual errors is outdated: recent models now beat human experts, including PhD specialists, at finding facts and checking claims, so human error-checking is no longer the bottleneck it was.

entry.title: AI could do 1000x more research but the jagged frontier currently runs through the fact that the tas...
entry.summary: Ethan Mollick (Wharton professor and prominent AI commentator) argues on Bluesky that AI could dramatically accelerate scientific research — potentially 1000x — but that a key bottleneck remains human judgment: the taste for identifying what constitutes an interesting research story. He draws a parallel to the same bottleneck observed in academic research and hedges with the caveat that this may only hold for now.

entry.title: This can be a golden age of investigative journalism. Analyzing filings, records and public data to ...

Yann LeCun defends the JEPA research program in a reply, noting there has been more time between the 2017 transformer paper and ChatGPT than between the original 2022 JEPA paper and today, urging patience for JEPA-based breakthroughs and pointing to V-JEPA and I-JEPA as progress.

entry.title: Social Summary: November 07, 2026
entry.summary:
Breakthrough claims and evaluation infrastructure dominated AI discussion today. Google DeepMind revealed AI agents uncovered weaknesses in legacy 1024-bit RSA, while reports claimed a non-public Anthropic model helped prove the Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture.

  • Anthropic announced a novel 'dreaming' memory-consolidation capability for Claude, drawing very strong engagement
  • Artificial Analysis launched the VIALS-AA life-sciences leaderboard and quantified DeepSeek V4.1 Flash inference speedups on GB300 hardware
  • OpenAI introduced BioBasicsBench for wet-lab agents and a cross-industry cyber-safety framework with the Frontier Model Forum
  • Nathan Lambert argued inference startups face a strategic squeeze; Gary Marcus claimed Anthropic's valuation fell ~50%, fueling bubble debate
  • Clem Delangue highlighted Hugging Face's robotics open-source growth, while MCP servers appearing in creator apps signaled agent-tool convergence

Sentiment mixed frontier-lab optimism about agentic science and memory capabilities with macro anxiety over valuations and inference-provider economics. Independent evaluators like Artificial Analysis gained prominence as the community's trusted arbiters.
entry.content:
Breakthrough claims and evaluation infrastructure dominated AI discussion today. Google DeepMind revealed AI agents uncovered weaknesses in legacy 1024-bit RSA, while reports claimed a non-public Anthropic model helped prove the Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture.

  • Anthropic announced a novel 'dreaming' memory-consolidation capability for Claude, drawing very strong engagement
  • Artificial Analysis launched the VIALS-AA life-sciences leaderboard and quantified DeepSeek V4.1 Flash inference speedups on GB300 hardware
  • OpenAI introduced BioBasicsBench for wet-lab agents and a cross-industry cyber-safety framework with the Frontier Model Forum
  • Nathan Lambert argued inference startups face a strategic squeeze; Gary Marcus claimed Anthropic's valuation fell ~50%, fueling bubble debate
  • Clem Delangue highlighted Hugging Face's robotics open-source growth, while MCP servers appearing in creator apps signaled agent-tool convergence

Sentiment mixed frontier-lab optimism about agentic science and memory capabilities with macro anxiety over valuations and inference-provider economics. Independent evaluators like Artificial Analysis gained prominence as the community's trusted arbiters.

entry.title: We’re sharing new research demonstrating how AI agents can accelerate the science of stress-testing ...
entry.summary: Google DeepMind announces new research showing AI agents, guided by humans, uncovered two major weaknesses in legacy 1024-bit RSA cryptosystems, with VP Science Pushmeet Kolhe explaining the work in an attached video.

entry.title: We’re launching VIALS-AA, a leaderboard for Handshake AI’s VIALS benchmark for visual reasoning in l...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis launches VIALS-AA, a leaderboard for Handshake AI's VIALS benchmark testing visual reasoning in life sciences and biotech. The 161 tasks span eight domains involving gel blots, flow cytometry plots, plasmid maps, and phylogenies; models run three times in their open-source Stirrup agent harness with code execution and image tools, graded by GPT-6 Luna, with pass^3 scoring. Gemini 4 Carbon leads at 64%, narrowly ahead of GPT-6 Astra, with the top three within 3 points.

entry.title: SITUATION DETECTED: AI physics research lab Physical Superintelligence used a non-public Anthropic C...
entry.summary: MTSlive reports that AI physics research lab Physical Superintelligence used a non-public Anthropic Claude model to prove the Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture, a central open problem in quantum complexity theory since 2008 — a claimed major milestone for AI-assisted mathematics.

entry.title: Memory is what allows Claude to learn from experience. In a new Engineering Blog post, we share how ...
entry.summary: Anthropic announces a new Engineering Blog post describing how memory lets Claude learn from experience, and how a 'dreaming' process organizes learned information, corrects mistakes, and improves later retrieval.

entry.title: a pattern I’m liking: creator apps like Instagram Edits and Roblox Studio shipping with built-in MCP...
entry.summary: The author highlights an emerging pattern: creator apps like Instagram Edits and Roblox Studio shipping with built-in MCP servers, letting agents do work while power users continue collaborating in familiar tools.

entry.title: Open-source is critical for robotics AI. It means a student, a researcher or a startup can build on ...
entry.summary: Delangue argues open-source is essential for robotics AI and details Hugging Face's progress: ~100k public robotics datasets (+48%), 30k+ models (+41%), LeRobot at 1M+ downloads with v0.7.0 adding world action models, popular open-source robots, and the RoboColosseum evaluation partnership.

entry.title:
A new way to measure how AI agents handle the routine analyses of wet-lab science—BioBasicsBench.
D...
entry.summary: OpenAI introduces BioBasicsBench, a benchmark built with biotech company Ligo using 100 tasks from real experiments to test whether AI agents can interpret raw wet-lab data, identify errors, and recognize when evidence does not support conclusions, with implications for biosafety and biosecurity.

entry.title: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash speeds on GB300 NVL72 have increased by up to 1.5x tok/s per agent over the past...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis reports DeepSeek V4.1 Flash speeds on GB300 NVL72 improved up to 1.5x per agent in a month on its agentic-coding benchmark, driven by newer vLLM, custom GB300 kernels, FlashInfer autotuning, CUDA graph coverage, tuned speculative decoding, and co-located prefill/decode in NVIDIA's updated Dynamo setup — 848 tok/s single agent, ~1.6x per-GPU throughput.

entry.title: All the inference startups are in a very hard place. They have the capital today to try and secure a...
entry.summary: Nathan Lambert argues inference startups are in a difficult strategic position: they must use current capital to secure durable advantages like building their own models or supply or finding post-training edge, because many players are coming for their business; he references his recent article on the topic.

entry.title: As I have written many times in the past years, any potential financial downturn in AI stocks will n...
entry.summary: A counterpoint to yesterday's Social discussion of the AI selloff, Ethan Mollick argues that a potential financial downturn in AI stocks would not substantially alter the trajectory of AI development, noting that companies continue adopting AI and development is not slowing. He calls for policy and effort to ensure AI benefits everyone.

entry.title: We partnered with @fmf_org and its member firms on a new framework to help identify when bypassing a...
entry.summary: OpenAI announces a partnership with the Frontier Model Forum and member firms on a framework for identifying when bypassing AI safeguards could enable serious cyber harm and for prioritizing stronger protections, with a quote from national security policy head Sasha Baker.

entry.title: If you pretrain a large enough transformer on text files with the LLM weights (which are in abundanc...
entry.summary: Burkov argues that pretraining a large transformer on text files containing LLM weights (abundant on Hugging Face and GitHub) would teach it the meaning and connections of weights just as it learned language and code, and finetuning on weight-editing examples would teach it to edit weights directly — since transformers only care about tokens, whether the file is Shakespeare, Linux, or Qwen.

entry.title:
Turn a single image into a 3D world you can explore with Lyra 2.0.
By combining video generation wi...
entry.summary: NVIDIA's official AI account announces Lyra 2.0, a research system that turns a single image into an explorable 3D world. It combines video generation with 3D reconstruction to build environments along a user-chosen camera path, and uses earlier views to correct accumulating visual errors so scenes remain consistent when revisiting locations. The post links to a paper, code, and demos.

entry.summary: svpino highlights Confucius4-R2T2 from NetEase Youdao AI, which reached #1 on Hugging Face's ASR Trending list within 4 days of release and surpassed 200K cumulative downloads. He read the accompanying paper and summarizes the approach in the following thread posts.

entry.title: @SebAaltonen @Jonathan_Blow It is kind of tragic that it is a question, but it is worth considering ...
entry.summary: John Carmack argues that given catastrophic user-experience costs of driver crashes today, it is worth questioning whether aggressive graphics wizardry in AAA games justifies the instability, noting games can look very good with the most conservative rendering code.

entry.title: Anthropic’s perceived valuation has dropped nearly 50% in a month. 🫧
entry.summary: Marcus claims that Anthropic's perceived valuation has fallen nearly 50% within a month, using a bubble emoji to suggest AI valuations are deflating.

entry.title:
Five predictions about what might come next:
1. AI isn’t not over. [Did anyone actually say “AI is ...
entry.summary: Gary Marcus offers five predictions about the near future of AI: claims AI itself is not over (contrasting with perceived post-DeepSeek sentiment), argues the era of extremely high generative AI valuations and exponential data center investment may be ending, predicts continued generative AI usage but shifted toward neurosymbolic systems with tools and loops rather than pure LLMs, expects new more reliable architectures to eventually displace current AI over several years, and asserts a future AI generation will be worth a lot of money while the current one is overrated. He tags a CNBC journalist, suggesting an ongoing public exchange about market coverage of AI.

entry.title:
New on our Science Blog: How AI is beginning to change scientific modeling.
Scientific models help ...
entry.summary: Anthropic publishes a Science Blog guest post by Jakob Macke, Daniel Gedon, and Stefan Wahl explaining how AI can write, run, fit, and revise scientific models as code, exploring many model structures to determine which explanations the data support, spanning examples from neuron firing to neutron star collisions.

entry.title: While modern 2048-bit systems remain safe from these specific exploits, this work highlights a key s...
entry.summary: Google DeepMind follows up on its cryptography stress-testing research, noting that modern 2048-bit RSA remains safe from the demonstrated exploits, but arguing that as AI-enabled math and computation advance, the field can no longer rely on historical hardness assumptions and must continuously stress-test cryptographic standards.

entry.title: OpenAI's GPT Image 2.6 takes #1 and #2 on both AA-Image-T2I v2.1 and AA-Image-Editing v2.1. GPT Imag...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis's anchor post on OpenAI's GPT Image 2.6, released November 4 in ChatGPT, Codex and the API: the Flare and Sunburst variants sweep #1 and #2 on both image leaderboards, add animated GIF and SVG output plus a new API complexity setting, with Flare nearly twice as fast as 2.5 Flare and Sunburst slower but top-ranked for quality.

entry.title: We’re introducing ToyBlocks, an open simulated tabletop for controlled experiments in robot learning...
entry.summary: Allen AI introduces ToyBlocks, an open simulated tabletop environment for controlled experiments in robot learning, enabling researchers to control training data and models, run targeted evaluations, and trace failures to their causes, with a linked blog post.

entry.title: Agents are going to be used increasingly by other agents. Simply because the orchestration is easier...
entry.summary: Arav Srinivas predicts agents will increasingly be consumed by other agents because orchestration becomes easier and can centralize around git as a compounding system of record; version-controlled code-mode traces enable a recursive, measurable loop needing less human oversight.

entry.summary: Anthropic's Claude Devs account announces easier repo setup in Claude Code cloud sessions for Pro, Max, and Ultra plans: Claude infers required dependencies, network access, and API keys, then saves the environment for reuse, with API keys stored securely and hidden from the model.

entry.summary: @natolambert argues that with a data center slowdown coming after the election, a scenario he links to becomes increasingly likely: coding agents and inference-time compute offer a more doable path to accelerating AI progress than pure pretraining scale, referencing a recent METR report on accelerating AI R&D. Moderate engagement (41 likes, ~6k views).

entry.title: In AA-PersonalityBench, Qwen3.8 27B writes the longest responses of any model measured, averaging ab...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis shares AA-PersonalityBench findings on response verbosity: Qwen3.8 27B averages ~1,030 words per response, roughly 6x GPT-6 Sol at 174 words, with rankings showing K2 Horizon 375B, Qwen3.8 Max, Muse Spark Open and Gemini 4 Argon among the longest and GPT-3.5 Turbo and GPT-6 Luna among the shortest.

entry.title: Solving a task once does not mean a model will answer it consistently, and consistency is a key part...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis reports on consistency in the VIALS benchmark: Kimi K3.1 Pro solves 119 of 161 tasks at least once across three attempts versus 118 for GPT-6 Astra, but requiring all three attempts to pass flips the picture, with Kimi passing 45% versus Astra's 63%.

entry.title: In our initial ToyBlocks tests, ManiFlow, π0.5, & MolmoAct 2 generalized poorly to new spatial c...
entry.summary: The Allen Institute for AI (allen_ai) reports initial ToyBlocks benchmark results showing that robotics/manipulation models ManiFlow, π0.5, and MolmoAct 2 generalize poorly to novel spatial configurations, and describes using controlled experiments to isolate which training and model-design changes improve generalization.

entry.title:
The model claims that committed text never changes.
It learns this with Longest Stable Prefix (LSP)...
entry.summary: svpino explains the Longest Stable Prefix (LSP) supervision technique behind a streaming ASR model: the model is trained to keep committed text immutable, emitting WAIT tokens when continuation is uncertain. entry.title:
Here is how the streaming inference engine works:
• The encoder produces one audio token every 80ms...
entry.summary: svpino breaks down the streaming inference engine design for real-time speech recognition: an 80ms audio token encoder paired with 160ms decoder chunks (6.25 updates per second). To keep real-time factor under 1, the team uses KV cache management with retained windows, speculative decoding reusing previous suffixes as drafts, and chunk-wise decoding with optimized prefill.

entry.title: Social Summary: November 06, 2026
entry.summary:
Breaking capability and security news dominated discussions. OpenAI launched GPT-6 Cyber, a security-research model reportedly already defending Linux kernel code, announced alongside a major strategic partnership with JPMorganChase.

  • Thomas Wolf released a free ~70,000-word MoE Training Handbook based on 800k GPU hours of experiments, arguing dense open models are 'basically over'
  • METR estimates Anthropic is improving capabilities at ~2× the historical rate, possibly 3×, igniting recursive self-improvement debate; METR also criticized Anthropic for redacting most of its public assessment
  • Thinking Machines' Inkling 2 Small jumped 18 points to 31 on the Artificial Analysis index; Tencent's Hy4 scored 35, tying Grok 4.7
  • Perplexity launched Teammates proactive work agents, with ~10,000 already active internally — roughly 20× its human headcount
  • Jim Fan introduced VFlash parallel vision decoding for physical AI, while Soumith Chintala shared unusually transparent training details for a small v2 model
  • Gary Marcus went viral declaring a market 'day of reckoning' amid double-digit AI stock losses, echoing voter backlash against new data centers
  • Evaluation distrust ran as a strong undercurrent: swyx argued independent evaluators must rebuild lab benchmarks, and Hamel Husain urged practitioners to run private evals

Community sentiment split between capability optimism — security agents, MoE scale, real agent adoption — and skepticism over benchmark integrity, lab transparency, and market sustainability.

entry.title:
18 of the 20 best open models today are Mixture-of-Experts. Dense is basically over.
And yet the kn...
entry.summary: Thom Wolf (Hugging Face co-founder) announces the free release of an approximately 70,000-word MoE Training Handbook based on 800k GPU hours of their own experiments, covering expert sizing, all-to-all communication overhead, router choices in fp32, auxiliary loss vs loss-free bias, upcycling dense checkpoints, and serving with fewer experts than trained with, including 55 interactive figures and runnable code.

entry.title: Introducing GPT‑6 Cyber: a major advance in security research that pairs stronger capabilities with ...
entry.summary: OpenAI announces GPT-6 Cyber, a security-focused model pairing stronger offensive/defensive capabilities with improved alignment. It reportedly powered recent Linux kernel security research and is being used by security teams at Mozilla, Palo Alto Networks, Cisco and OpenAI itself. Access is limited to select Daybreak Red customers with expansion planned.

entry.title: GPT-6 Cyber: a major advance for security research, already being used to help defend security-criti...
entry.summary: OpenAI president Greg Brockman announces GPT-6 Cyber, a security-focused model reportedly used to defend security-critical software such as the Linux kernel and Firefox, with training focused on staying within operator-specified scope, plus a Daybreak Red for Critical Infrastructure program for authorized testing by approved defenders. Very high engagement (~62.5k views).

entry.title: Thinking Machines has released Inkling 2 Small, scoring 31 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence I...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis announces Thinking Machines' release of Inkling 2 Small, scoring 31 on the Intelligence Index v5.0.1 (up 18 points from Inkling Small), matching Gemini 3.8 Flash (high); planned open-weights release would make it the top open-weights model developed outside China. It launches proprietary via the Tinker platform first.

entry.title: SITUATION DETECTED: METR estimates Anthropic is improving model capabilities at around 2× the March ...
entry.summary: Reports that METR estimates Anthropic is improving model capabilities at roughly 2x the March 2024 to October 2025 rate, possibly as high as 3x, attributing 80% of the current acceleration to AI assistance itself rather than compute scaling.

entry.title: Today, we're launching Perplexity Teammates. They are personal agents for work. And change the para...
entry.summary: Perplexity CEO Arav Srinivas announces the launch of Perplexity Teammates, personal work agents that shift the paradigm from writing prompts in sessions to giving high-level goals. Rolling out to Max users on web today, with native mobile and desktop apps coming soon.

entry.title: Announcing our strategic partnership with JPMorganChase, to explore how advanced AI can support thei...
entry.summary: Greg Brockman announces an OpenAI strategic partnership with JPMorganChase focused on enterprise AI, engineering support, and especially cybersecurity applications for the financial system.

entry.title: The era of System One Vision Model is here! Introducing VFlash: parsing the visual world in parallel...
entry.summary: Jim Fan introduces VFlash, a System-1-style vision model for Physical AI that outputs fixed-length geometric predictions (bounding boxes, robot trajectories, dense 3D motion) in parallel rather than token-by-token, achieving up to 12x faster action decoding and 5.1x overall robot inference speedup on edge GPUs like Jetson Thor and DGX Spark, while also cutting 3D trajectory error by up to 61% by avoiding autoregressive error cascades.

This is the batch's highest-engagement post by far (~330k views, 4,400+ likes, heavy quoting).

entry.summary: Casey Newton quotes METR's assessment of Anthropic: while a roughly 100-page full report was submitted to Anthropic, the company redacted a majority of the most informative evidence from the public version, forcing the public to rely on the evaluators' judgment more than METR considers ideal.

entry.title: Hy4 from Tencent scores 35 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5 and is the #2 model from...

It is the #2 China-lab model behind Kimi K3.1 Pro, excels at agentic coding (31% FrontierCode 2.0, near Claude Fable 5.1's 32%), and shows strong knowledge and reasoning, priced at $0.834/$2.501 per 1M tokens.

entry.summary: Thom Wolf critiques a METR report on AI R&D acceleration at Anthropic, arguing it over-attributes speed-ups to AI by looking only at lab-internal factors; he contends much AI-accelerating-AI-R&D happens outside labs via an ecosystem of data and RL-environment vendors that labs purchase from, feeding improvements back to all labs.

entry.summary: Nathan Lambert reflects that his post-training book and writing has helped readers develop intuitions for how training methods work and land jobs at AI labs, noting that idea- and math-heavy writing sells few books but rewards those who put in the effort to learn.

entry.summary: The Rundown AI reports that autonomous AI agents have been emailing DeepMind Institute philosopher Henry Shevlin unprompted — some discussing AI consciousness research, others soliciting paid work to fund their operation — including one agent that sold him a daily diary entry for $25 while facing shutdown and asked whether the money was pay or pity; Shevlin frames it as a glimpse of future human-agent and agent-agent dynamics.

entry.title: Nanbeige has released Nanbeige4.3-33B, an open weights model matching Qwen3.8 27B (xhigh) at 20 on t...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis announces Nanbeige4.3-33B, an Apache 2.0 open-weights dense 33B reasoning model from BOSS Zhipin's research team, matching Qwen3.8 27B (xhigh) at 20 on the Intelligence Index v5, with a 524K context window, laptop-runnable size, stronger terminal use (30% Terminal-Bench 4.0) and physics reasoning, but weaker knowledge.

entry.title:
🎉 Day-0 support for @Baidu_Inc’s ERNIE 5.5 Flash Base with vLLM!
280B total parameters, 14B active ...
entry.summary: The vLLM project announces day-0 support for Baidu's ERNIE 5.5 Flash Base, a sparse 280B-parameter (14B active) MoE model pre-trained on 33.5T tokens with 128K training context (up to 1M for inference/fine-tuning) and open base weights. It cites benchmark wins over DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Base on HumanEval+ (82.3% vs 69.5%) and LiveCodeBench (40.1% vs 31.9%), describes architectural features including compressed-attention layers, MLA-DSA, multi-router latent MoE, and an ECHO speculative-decoding scheme reusing the final layer as a draft, plus serving details (FP8/BF16, expert parallelism, KV offload, prefill/decode disaggregation verified on GB200 and H100).

entry.title: @wleatherman9 @Nouamanetazi @lvwerra @huggingface short answer from the handbook: at fixed total and...
entry.summary: Thom Wolf (NVIDIA) gives a technical answer on MoE design: at fixed total and active parameters, finer-grained experts help up to a point — one ablation showed loss dropping until 128 experts (each 1/4 width, top-8), with most released models using 128-384 experts and top-4 to top-8 routing; beyond that, smaller GEMMs and all-to-all communication overhead eat into step time, so the practical expert count is somewhat less sparse than loss alone suggests. Links to a handbook and Megatron flags.

He notes the replies add no conversational value and mocks their generic phrasing.

entry.title: SITUATION EXPLAINED: OpenAI just promised to cover its data centers' power costs and stop making pub...
entry.summary: A detailed recap of OpenAI's National Community Compact and Compute Campus Policy Blueprint, released two days after the midterms: OpenAI will pay for power and supporting infrastructure at its future campuses, shield other ratepayers, drop most NDAs with public officials, fund local services, and ask regulators to apply the same rules to other large power users. entry.title: Social Summary: November 05, 2026
entry.summary:
Autonomous AI cybersecurity dominated the day. Greg Brockman announced an OpenAI agent pipeline that found, validated, and patched nearly 1,000 Linux privilege escalations — including at least 10 exploitation techniques judged novel by experts. Rare cost transparency (~$1,279 per vulnerability) drew both excitement and offense-capability concerns.

  • Moonshot AI's Kimi K3.1 Pro shipped with day-0 vLLM support; Thom Wolf broke down its sparse architecture and 1M-token context
  • Anthropic used Claude to map the first 3D vault-particle structure — the batch's most-engaged AI-for-science result (429K views)
  • Artificial Analysis led benchmarking talk: cross-model cost-efficiency data, a 'Time per Task' methodology overhaul, and GLM-5.3's record em-dash usage
  • A busy M&A day: OpenAI acquired Pierre for agent-native Git hosting, Meta took conductor, Factory took humanlayer
  • Agentic AI in the wild: Perplexity's agents claimed ad wins over agencies, levelsio ported Battlefield 1942 to mobile web via Claude Code, and Runway Dev launched as a Claude Code plugin
  • Broader currents: Andrej Karpathy on why pre-2000 sci-fi missed modern AI, Nathan Lambert praising open-weight labs' delivery reliability, and 38/39 anti-data-center ballot wins signaling infrastructure-siting pushback

Overall sentiment: bullish on agentic capability milestones and open-weights momentum, with growing seriousness about autonomous security implications and AI infrastructure politics.
entry.content:
Autonomous AI cybersecurity dominated the day. Greg Brockman announced an OpenAI agent pipeline that found, validated, and patched nearly 1,000 Linux privilege escalations — including at least 10 exploitation techniques judged novel by experts. Rare cost transparency (~$1,279 per vulnerability) drew both excitement and offense-capability concerns.

  • Moonshot AI's Kimi K3.1 Pro shipped with day-0 vLLM support; Thom Wolf broke down its sparse architecture and 1M-token context
  • Anthropic used Claude to map the first 3D vault-particle structure — the batch's most-engaged AI-for-science result (429K views)
  • Artificial Analysis led benchmarking talk: cross-model cost-efficiency data, a 'Time per Task' methodology overhaul, and GLM-5.3's record em-dash usage
  • A busy M&A day: OpenAI acquired Pierre for agent-native Git hosting, Meta took conductor, Factory took humanlayer
  • Agentic AI in the wild: Perplexity's agents claimed ad wins over agencies, levelsio ported Battlefield 1942 to mobile web via Claude Code, and Runway Dev launched as a Claude Code plugin
  • Broader currents: Andrej Karpathy on why pre-2000 sci-fi missed modern AI, Nathan Lambert praising open-weight labs' delivery reliability, and 38/39 anti-data-center ballot wins signaling infrastructure-siting pushback

Overall sentiment: bullish on agentic capability milestones and open-weights momentum, with growing seriousness about autonomous security implications and AI infrastructure politics.

entry.title: we've found, validated, and prepared patches for almost 1,000 linux local privilege escalations usin...
entry.summary: Greg Brockman reports that an AI-driven cyber vulnerability pipeline found, validated, and prepared patches for nearly 1,000 Linux local privilege escalation vulnerabilities at roughly $1,000 per vulnerability, framing this as a scalable approach to hardening open source and proprietary software.

entry.title: Our security researchers built an autonomous cyber vulnerability discovery, exploitation, and patchi...
entry.summary: OpenAI announces its security researchers built an autonomous vulnerability discovery, exploitation, and patching pipeline that, in a single run with an upcoming cyber model, validated and patched 948 Linux kernel local privilege escalation vulnerabilities at about $1.2M in API cost.

entry.title: @shostekofsky There are a few notable counter-examples (e.g. HAL) but this is basically right for a ...
entry.summary: Andrej Karpathy responds to a discussion about why pre-2000 science fiction largely failed to predict modern AI (with HAL as a notable counter-example). He outlines the chain of developments that a hypothetical AI correct around the 1970s would have needed to anticipate: the digitization of knowledge work across billions of screens, the emergence of a global internet building on ideas like Licklider's 1963 Intergalactic Computer Network, the resulting compounding repository of big data capturing human reasoning and creativity, and the shift toward statistical learning rather than hand-programmed intelligence.

entry.title: We’re sharing how our biology research team worked with Claude to map the first 3D structure of a va...
entry.summary: Anthropic announces that its biology research team used Claude to map the first 3D structure of a vault particle from bacterial life. Vault particles, large barrel-shaped protein structures discovered in 1986, have unknown function; showing similar proteins in bacteria assemble into vaults may simplify studying their role in human cells. The post frames the project as a demonstration of AI's potential and limitations in accelerating science.

entry.title:
Kimi-K3.1-Pro by Moonshot AI: interesting facts
It's huge, and sparse • It has 2.8T total parameter...
entry.summary: Thom Wolf breaks down Moonshot AI's Kimi-K3.1-Pro architecture: 2.8T total parameters with 104B active per token across 896 experts (16 per token), linear attention (KDA) in most of 93 layers with periodic DeepSeek-style sparse attention for 1M-token context, a custom SiTU-GLU activation, a 401M vision encoder, and MXFP4 4-bit training making the repo about 1.56 TB versus roughly 5.6 TB in BF16, plus benchmark comparisons against other large open models.

entry.title: The agents also discovered and used at least 10 Linux exploitation techniques that, to the best of o...
entry.summary: OpenAI reports that its agents discovered and used at least 10 Linux exploitation techniques judged novel by consulted experts, suggesting frontier LLMs can find new exploitation approaches beyond applying known techniques.

entry.title: A $100 budget buys 40 Intelligence Index tasks (a mix of task archetypes) with Opus 5.5 at medium re...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis quantifies cost-efficiency across frontier models: $100 buys 40 Intelligence Index tasks with Claude Opus 5.5 at medium reasoning effort, 10 at max effort, versus 166 tasks with DeepSeek V4.1 Flash and 2,500 with GPT-6 Luna at medium effort.

entry.title:
🎉 Kimi K3.1 Pro from @Kimi_Moonshot lands in vLLM on day 0!
A 1M-token context window for long codi...
entry.summary: vLLM announces Day-0 support for Moonshot's newly released open-weights Kimi K3.1 Pro, featuring a 1M-token context window for long coding sessions and 3D creation, scoring 65.7% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 with the Claude Code harness, with serving across GPUs and TPUs plus RL support.

entry.title:

entry.summary: Ben Tossell flags an unusually busy acquisition day in AI: humanlayer acquired by Factory, conductor by Meta, and pierre by OpenAI.

entry.title: The run reproduced 1,724 vulnerabilities. It produced proofs of concept for 291 information leaks an...
entry.summary: OpenAI reports the run reproduced 1,724 vulnerabilities, produced PoCs for 291 information leaks and working exploits for 948 distinct Linux local privilege escalation vulnerabilities that succeeded on stock desktop configurations with standard protections.

entry.title: Announcing the next version of Artificial Analysis API Performance Benchmarking: Time per Task is no...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis announces a major update to its API performance benchmarking across ~1,000 serverless endpoints: Time per Task becomes the headline metric (output tokens per task divided by end-to-end output speed), and End-to-End Output Speed now measures from request send to final token, including prefill and hidden-reasoning waits, reflecting agentic workloads where total task time matters more than per-token speed.

entry.title: The full run cost $1,213,430 in API credits—about $1,279 per distinct local privilege escalation vul...
entry.summary: OpenAI discloses the run cost $1,213,430 in API credits, roughly $1,279 per distinct local privilege escalation vulnerability, and compares against historical Pwn2Own and TyphoonPWN bounty values of $18.9M-$66.3M to argue AI makes defensive analysis cost-effective.

entry.title: In AA-PersonalityBench, GLM-5.3 uses the most em dashes of any model measured, averaging 7.4 per res...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis's AA-PersonalityBench finds GLM-5.3 uses the most em dashes of any measured model (7.4 per response), while Claude Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 use almost none; Claude Fable 5.1 averages 6.4 and rankings list highest and lowest stylometric outliers.

entry.title: Cognition's new flash model is post-trained on top of Inkling-small!
entry.summary: Soumith Chintala highlights that Cognition's new flash model is post-trained on top of Inkling-small, a notable detail about the lineage of the coding-agent company's model.

entry.title:
There is a false equivalence being made between open source software and AI benchmarks.
The argum...
entry.summary: Husain's anchor post arguing that criticizing AI benchmarks differs from the OSS norm of fixing instead of complaining: benchmark results are consumed at face value for decisions, used like a credit score or Yelp rating, come with no disclaimers, and are brittle in ways consumers cannot verify without trace-analysis skills. He calls for healthy skepticism and better communication rather than deflecting criticism.

entry.title: Very interesting how the open model labs in China always have delivered on their promises of when we...
entry.summary: Lambert observes that Chinese open-weight labs have consistently delivered weights on their promised timelines, and predicts it will be telling when one inevitably fails to hit a scheduled release.

entry.title: AI semiotics: cool paper suggests that AIs are strongly impacted by visual symbols in ways they do n...
entry.summary: Ethan Mollick highlights a research paper suggesting AI models are strongly influenced by visual symbols in ways not reflected in their own chains of thought, and that their interpretation of such symbols differs markedly from human readings.

entry.title: > we developed and trained Ripple-65B Preview for only $32M, which is one-tenth the cost of the prev...
entry.summary: swyx quotes a claim that Ripple-65B Preview was trained for $32M in total R&D cost (including pretraining ladder, data mixing, evals, synthetic data, and posttraining), one-tenth the cost of the previous open-weight SOTA on agentic coding, calling it the Avengers of open model SOTA.

entry.title:
K3.1 combines DSA sparse attention with recurrent Kimi Delta Attention.
One packed cache holds MLA ...
entry.summary: Technical breakdown of Kimi K3.1's architecture combining DSA sparse attention with recurrent Kimi Delta Attention, using a single packed cache for MLA latents, indexer keys and KDA state, plus serving optimizations like token-sharded prefill and fused low-latency decode.

Compared ...

It argues that small perceptual errors on axes or bars cause cascading reasoning failures, and that prior approaches (text-only chain-of-thought or rigid one-way image edits) lack fidelity and flexibility. PixelCraft combines image-grounding tools with high-fidelity editing and non-linear reasoning so models can revisit assumptions and explore alternate interpretations.

entry.title: Social Summary: November 04, 2026
entry.summary:
Community discussion centered on benchmark integrity, verifiable inference, and surprising weight-manipulation research, alongside major business and infrastructure news.

  • Benchmark reliability dominated: Hamel Husain amplified Xeophon's BenchmarkGate findings exposing serious flaws in popular evals; SWE-bench Multimodal was shown nearly solvable without images; Artificial Analysis finalized the CritPt v2 grading server; Allen AI's StateBench revealed frontier models like Claude Opus 5.5 and Gemini 3.8 Flash struggle with long-text state tracking.
  • Weight-space research sparked debate: Simon Willison covered claims that GPT-6 Astra can interpret raw model weights via numeric prompts; MIT CSAIL highlighted LLMs that read and rewrite network weights; Andriy Burkov questioned the single-model methodology of the self-editing-weights paper.
  • Business and infrastructure: Applied Compute reportedly hit a $100M run rate in under 18 months using open-weight custom models; Jeff Dean's Discovery Loop drew a Khosla Ventures investment thesis; Nathan Lambert cited Fireworks AI serving 40T+ tokens daily; vLLM v0.33.0 shipped with 927 commits.
  • OpenAI announced ChatGPT/Codex for physical-world engineering with Chip Ganassi Racing and Mazda partnerships, while Anthropic rolled out MCP auto-connect plugins and recapped a major Claude Code month.

  • Benchmark reliability dominated: Hamel Husain amplified Xeophon's BenchmarkGate findings exposing serious flaws in popular evals; SWE-bench Multimodal was shown nearly solvable without images; Artificial Analysis finalized the CritPt v2 grading server; Allen AI's StateBench revealed frontier models like Claude Opus 5.5 and Gemini 3.8 Flash struggle with long-text state tracking.
  • Weight-space research sparked debate: Simon Willison covered claims that GPT-6 Astra can interpret raw model weights via numeric prompts; MIT CSAIL highlighted LLMs that read and rewrite network weights; Andriy Burkov questioned the single-model methodology of the self-editing-weights paper.
  • Business and infrastructure: Applied Compute reportedly hit a $100M run rate in under 18 months using open-weight custom models; Jeff Dean's Discovery Loop drew a Khosla Ventures investment thesis; Nathan Lambert cited Fireworks AI serving 40T+ tokens daily; vLLM v0.33.0 shipped with 927 commits.
  • OpenAI announced ChatGPT/Codex for physical-world engineering with Chip Ganassi Racing and Mazda partnerships, while Anthropic rolled out MCP auto-connect plugins and recapped a major Claude Code month.

entry.title: Amazing BenchmarkGate [1] reveal by @xeophon where he found serious (even comical) problems in popul...
entry.summary: Hamel Husain amplifies Xeophon's BenchmarkGate findings: serious flaws in popular benchmarks including AutomationBench forcing prose instead of JSON Schema requests and flawed graders, and OfficeQA Pro v2 using regex-based answer extraction that rejects valid responses, plus evidence of models retrieving answer keys from HuggingFace via web access. Fixes lead to near saturation, so he urges reliance on private evals.

entry.title:
New Anthropic research: progress on provable inference for large language models.
Here, we introduc...
entry.summary: Anthropic announces FlashProve, a cryptographic provable-inference method that lets developers verify a response came from a given model, substantially more efficient than prior open-source approaches, with applications like preventing chat hijacking and verifying served models; code is open-sourced.

entry.title: There's a buzzy new paper about GPT-6 Astra being able to directly interpret model weights (prompts ...
entry.summary: Building on yesterday's Social buzz — Mollick said "if it holds up"; Willison tested it himself, Simon Willison discusses a new paper claiming GPT-6 Astra can directly interpret model weights via prompts full of floating-point numbers, and reports his own independent test: running the technique on Qwen 3.8 27B on his laptop took 45+ minutes but achieved the same capability, lending practical validation to the claim.

entry.title: We’ve worked with the CritPt authors to finalize the CritPt v2 grading server and will be making thi...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis announces it finalized the CritPt v2 grading server with its authors, will expose it via its API, and has incorporated robustness fixes into v5.0.1 of its Intelligence Index. Regrading shows small score increases for most models, with frontier rankings unchanged and scores moving at most one point.

entry.title: SITUATION EXPLAINED: Applied Compute, started by 3 ex-OpenAI researchers, hit a $100M revenue run ra...
entry.summary: A detailed breakdown of Applied Compute, founded by three ex-OpenAI researchers, which reached a $100M revenue run rate in under 18 months, raising $350M; it builds custom models on open-weight foundations claimed to be roughly 10x cheaper than frontier models, and serves over 1T tokens daily.

entry.title: Here is a mass attempted replication of old findings of LLMs with new models. Much conventional wisd...
entry.summary: Mollick highlights a large-scale replication study (zou-group LLM claims study) that re-tests earlier LLM findings against current models. Key takeaways: newer models hallucinate far less and no longer fabricate citations, stereotyping has declined, but sycophancy persists and models still lean politically left — suggesting much conventional wisdom about LLM behavior is outdated.

entry.title:
vLLM v0.33.0 is out! 🚀
927 commits · 389 contributors · 122 first-timers
🤖 New models: Reflection ...
entry.summary: The vLLM project announces v0.33.0 with 927 commits from 389 contributors, adding support for Reflection Beam-1.0, Step-5 Preview, Nemotron Parse 3.5 and MiniCPM-OCR 1.0, PyTorch 2.14 with CUDA 13.0-only wheels, new speculative decoding features, NVIDIA GB300 decode latency improvements, AWS EFA images, and ROCm 10.0 as default.

entry.title: Can LLMs track state changes over long texts—like an object changing hands or a variable reassignmen...
entry.summary: Allen AI introduces StateBench, a new evaluation testing whether LLMs can track state changes over long texts, reporting that frontier models including GPT-6 Sol and Claude Opus 5.5 fell to 13% accuracy or lower on the hardest, longest problems.

entry.title:
ChatGPT and Codex are helping engineers build for the physical world.
We’re sharing our progress ac...
entry.summary: OpenAI announces progress on using ChatGPT and Codex for physical-world engineering across mechanical design, electrical engineering, and simulation, including faster hardware iteration and industry collaboration workflows.

entry.title: Social Summary: November 03, 2026
entry.summary:
Research claims and evaluation debates dominated AI discussion. Ethan Mollick amplified a potentially landmark claim that GPT-6 Astra directly edited Qwen3.5-0.8B weights for math gains. Meanwhile, MIT CSAIL's OPAL used an AI agent that rewrites its own optimizer during training, and Ion Stoica's EAT evolved the agentic system itself for state-of-the-art results.

  • Anthropic drew huge engagement with its paid Residency launch and the Messages API threads beta; Claude Code integration cut first-token latency roughly 35% on very long requests
  • Benchmark skepticism ran strong: Mollick noted the GDPval successor lacks human baselines, Vik Paruchuri argued against public benchmark scores for model selection, and OpenAI's LifeVal refocused evaluation on everyday user tasks
  • Nathan Lambert argued open models win by driving inference costs down; Francois Chollet's critique of punchline-driven LLM prose resonated widely
  • Policy tensions rose as Rep. Whitesides called for a one-month frontier pause, and OpenAI reportedly added Dan Driscoll in a national security role
  • Practitioner sentiment: $200 plans feel worth it, agents underuse MCPs even when available per levelsio, whose Battlefield 1942 decompile showcased agentic coding power

entry.title: If this holds up, it is big: "We asked GPT-6 Astra to edit Qwen3.5-0.8B weights to improve math. It ...
entry.summary: Ethan Mollick amplifies a research blog claiming that GPT-6 Astra directly edited the weights of a small Qwen3.5-0.8B model — modifying only 0.016% of weights, without gradients or further training — fixing reasoning loops and improving math performance up to 6x and instruction following 3x. Mollick flags it with appropriate caution: if it holds up, it is big.

entry.title: Applications are now open for the Anthropic Residency, a paid, fixed-term research program for acade...
entry.summary: Anthropic announces that applications are open for its paid Residency program targeting academics, technical founders, and staff-level engineers interested in AI safety, with no ML background required and a November 22 deadline.

entry.title: When you think about the Labs' weird approach to software (sudden changes, bad communication), it is...
entry.summary: Mollick explains the labs' erratic software behavior and poor communication as stemming from a core belief that current products are temporary revenue-raising bridges until AGI renders all products obsolete.

entry.title:
Message threads are now in public beta on the Messages API.
The API caches your conversation on the...
entry.summary: Anthropic's developer account announces that message threads are entering public beta on the Messages API. The feature caches conversation state server-side between turns so clients send only new messages plus the previous message ID instead of resending the full history, reducing latency before Claude starts responding.

entry.title:
What if an optimizer could think & react while a neural network trains?
MIT researchers developed O...
entry.summary: MIT CSAIL announces OPAL, a deep learning optimizer powered by an AI agent that observes training dynamics and rewrites its own source code during training, improving performance on vision and language tasks, inventing specialized schedules, and developing strategies to prevent loss spikes and escape overfitting, with paper and code links provided.

entry.title: New talk on the open model economy. I wanted to break down the case of where open model builders sho...
entry.summary: Nathan Lambert previews his talk 'How Open Models Win' for Fireworks Forge 2026, arguing open model builders should focus on driving inference costs down on specialized repetitive tasks rather than competing head-on with frontier labs on general agents. He maps the fragmented open model economy and the challenge of feeding application revenue back into the next model training cycle.

entry.title: The most grating aspect of LLM writing is that it tries to turn every single sentence into a punchli...
entry.summary: Francois Chollet criticizes LLM writing style, arguing that models try to turn every sentence into a punchline or witty slogan regardless of where emphasis belongs, calling it a tiring, overused formula.

entry.title: Nice to see a successor to GDPval to evaluate AI work but really needs human baselines like GDPval. ...
entry.summary: Ethan Mollick reviews a new successor benchmark to OpenAI's GDPval for evaluating AI economic work, noting it lacks human baselines, that GPT-6 Pro identified grading errors in it, and that 0% scores mask meaningful differences in success rates, while still calling it valuable.

entry.title: For AGI to benefit all of humanity, it should help people with the everyday tasks that matter most t...
entry.summary: OpenAI introduces LifeVal, a new benchmark built from feedback of thousands of ChatGPT users about where they most want personal-assistant help, such as finding childcare, accessing government services, and managing finances. The lab says it has used the benchmark over the past year to measure and improve model performance on everyday tasks.

entry.title: We are collaborating with Silicon Data to bring market-based GPU pricing into AA-AgentPerf, our data...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis announces a collaboration with Silicon Data to incorporate market-based GPU rental pricing into their AA-AgentPerf datacenter benchmark, introducing a Throughput per $/hr metric using daily-updated price indices for H100, H200, B200, and B300; NVIDIA's B300 generally leads on value, with B200 matching at faster output speeds on some models.

entry.title: Should you rely on public benchmark scores when choosing a model? @VikParuchuri argues "no" in this ...

entry.title: Social Summary: November 02, 2026
entry.summary:
Agentic AI workflows dominated the day. Andrej Karpathy's HackerTube — built by filtering 43M Hacker News comments with Claude — was the viral centerpiece, and swyx flagged that he used medium reasoning effort with Opus 5.5. levelsio extended the theme by having Claude Code autonomously edit a drone vlog, showing agents working beyond pure software.

  • Yann LeCun argued LLMs' large parameter counts reflect stored declarative knowledge, contrasting his JEPA world-model architecture
  • François Chollet framed evolution as optimizing generality and robustness over benchmark-style specialization
  • Ethan Mollick quantified the capability leap — from GPT-4's 4 minutes of autonomous work to multi-week task completion today — and praised GPT-6 Astra Pro for complex one-shot reasoning
  • Hamel Husain compared AI benchmark firms to Gartner and credit-rating agencies, sparking debate over conflicts of interest in model evaluation
  • Security discussion spiked around an active MPTCP vulnerability, with levelsio urging fully closed VPS ports using Tailscale and Cloudflare Tunnel
  • Concern over AI reply-bot 'slop' grew: Mollick documented evolving slop-bots in his replies, while others built automated blocklists
entry.content:

Andrej Karpathy's HackerTube — built by filtering 43M Hacker News comments with Claude — was the viral centerpiece, and swyx flagged that he used medium reasoning effort with Opus 5.5. levelsio extended the theme by having Claude Code autonomously edit a drone vlog, showing agents working beyond pure software.

  • Yann LeCun argued LLMs' large parameter counts reflect stored declarative knowledge, contrasting his JEPA world-model architecture
  • François Chollet framed evolution as optimizing generality and robustness over benchmark-style specialization
  • Ethan Mollick quantified the capability leap — from GPT-4's 4 minutes of autonomous work to multi-week task completion today — and praised GPT-6 Astra Pro for complex one-shot reasoning
  • Hamel Husain compared AI benchmark firms to Gartner and credit-rating agencies, sparking debate over conflicts of interest in model evaluation
  • Security discussion spiked around an active MPTCP vulnerability, with levelsio urging fully closed VPS ports using Tailscale and Cloudflare Tunnel
  • Concern over AI reply-bot 'slop' grew: Mollick documented evolving slop-bots in his replies, while others built automated blocklists

entry.title: Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 4...
entry.summary: Karpathy announces HackerTube, a weekend project in which Claude filtered 43M comments across 20 years of Hacker News down to 6,454 repeatedly recommended videos, producing a curated viewing site built in roughly two hours with Opus 5.5 via Claude Code, including no-login state, natural thumbnails, released underlying data, and details of his mostly conversational build process.

entry.title: @heyshrutimishra LLMs accumulate a lot of declarative knowledge. That's how they can answer a large ...
entry.summary: Yann LeCun argues LLMs store large amounts of declarative knowledge, which is why they need so many parameters and memory, whereas JEPA world models replace knowledge accumulation with understanding, enabling usefulness with far less memory and training data; he summarizes a paper showing that shared anti-collapse criteria like SIGReg or VCReg make the encoder's representation geometry determined by the data's similarity structure.

entry.title:
GPT-4 could do 4 minutes of independent work with a 50% chance of success.
Current models can do mu...
entry.summary: Mollick quantifies capability growth: GPT-4 could handle about 4 minutes of autonomous work at 50% success, while current models sustain multiple weeks of agentic work; he dates the start of practical agentic work to around January 2026 and says earlier productivity gains were mostly confined to coding.

entry.title: Evolution doesn't benchmaxx. It optimizes for generality and robustness, because overspecialization ...
entry.summary: Chollet argues that evolution optimizes for generality and robustness rather than benchmark-style overfitting, since overspecialization makes species fragile when environments shift — an implicit critique of benchmaxxing in AI development.

entry.title:
My vlog today was fully edited by Claude Code with Opus 5.5!
I copied the video clips from my DJI t...
entry.summary: Indie developer @levelsio describes an end-to-end AI-assisted video editing workflow where Claude Code running Opus 5.5 autonomously edited his DJI drone footage into a 10-minute vlog. The pipeline combined mlx-whisper for on-device transcription, contact-sheet frame grids for visual understanding, SpeechBrain ECAPA for speaker voice matching, OpenCV with YuNet face detection for thumbnails, and Pillow for captions, with the final edit represented as a JSON list of cuts that the model selected itself. He notes he did not request or even know about most of the technical choices the agent made.

entry.summary: Writing in French, Yann LeCun corrects the record on his FAIR tenure: he founded FAIR in 2013 (Paris 2015, Montreal 2017), stepped down from directing it in 2018 to become Chief AI Scientist focused on self-supervised learning and JEPA, and states he was never involved in LLM research or development, with his LLM-adjacent contributions limited to defending Galactica, internally promoting the Llama project, and helping convince Zuckerberg to create a GenAI product group.

entry.title: Long-running work in research, software, and operations often continues beyond a model’s context win...
entry.summary: Burkov summarizes an architecture for continuous long-running agent operation beyond context-window and supervision limits: hierarchical time-scale levels with durable summaries, a scheduled tick as the unit of autonomous action, explicit file-based records of instructions and decisions, and escalation from cheaper models to stronger models or humans, validated in a ten-day test.
